newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower ahead of long weekend.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower on Thursday as investors took profits ahead of a three-day weekend in Switzerland.
"People prefered to take profits ahead of U.S. figures on Friday and the long weekend," one dealer said.
Friday is Swiss national day and the bourse will be closed.
One dealer said U.S. data on Thursday, including preliminary Q2 GDP, showed a slowdown of economic growth. "But some people were hoping for a more clear slowdown," he added.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slid 31.3 points or 0.53 percent to 5,898.2 points.
The all-share Swiss Peformance Index (SPI) was down 15.31 points at 3,752.66.
Bourse volume was a modest 2.07 billion Swiss francs.
Dealers said developments at the start of next week would largely depend on U.S. and European markets on Friday.
Volume-leader Novartis, whose Wednesday rise of three percent pulled the market up, was hit by profit taking but rebounded to close one franc lower at 2,427 Swiss francs.

Dealers said the stock received a late boost after Novartis said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) had given it clearance to market Femara, a new medication for treating advanced breast cancer.
Industrials saw bigger losses, including Roche, Alusuisse, ABB, Sulzer, Ciba SC and Clariant.
The Alusuisse-Lonza Group said it had acquired ACI Rockware Ltd from the Rockware Group Ltd and BTR Industries Ltd, a subsidiary of BTR Plc, for an undisclosed amount.

Shares of temporary employment firm Adecco fell 31 francs to 589. The company said after the bourse closed that group net before goodwill amortisation rose 36 percent to 129.2 million Swiss francs in the first half year, but the operating margin decreased to 4.0 pct vs 4.2 pct.
Banks were lower ahead of today's New York court hearing on class-action suits by Holocaust victims and heirs. UBS gave up 16 francs to 1,684.
No ruling was expected on Thursday. Dealers said the sector could witness a rally next week after the insecurity ahead of the hearing is over.
Insurers Zurich and Swiss Life saw solid demand. Swiss Life advanced 42 francs to 855.
